### PART A - Creating Vectors and List

Question 1: A factory has a census of its workers. There are 50 workers in total. The following list shows their ages: `34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24,33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18.

a. Create a vector for the worker’s age.

```{r}
# Store the ages of the 50 factory workers in a vector
ages <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 
          35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 
          50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 
          35, 24, 33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 
          48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)

# Verify total count
length(ages)

# Five-number summary (Min, 1st Qu, Median, Mean, 3rd Qu, Max)
summary(ages)

# Additional statistical measurements
mean_age   <- mean(ages)
median_age <- median(ages)
sd_age     <- sd(ages)
range_age  <- range(ages)

# Print specific results
cat("Mean Age:", mean_age, "\n")
cat("Median Age:", median_age, "\n")
cat("Standard Deviation:", sd_age, "\n")
cat("Age Range:", range_age[1], "to", range_age[2], "\n")

# Optional: Create a visual distribution histogram
hist(ages, 
     main = "Distribution of Factory Workers' Ages",
     xlab = "Age", 
     ylab = "Number of Workers",
     col = "steelblue", 
     border = "white")
```
b. How many data points?

Answer: 50 data points

c. Find the minimum and the maximum value of worker’s age.

```{r}
# Ages vector
ages <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 
          35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 
          50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 
          35, 24, 33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 
          48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)

# Calculate minimum and maximum
min_age <- min(ages)
max_age <- max(ages)

# Print the results
cat("Minimum Age:", min_age, "\n")
cat("Maximum Age:", max_age, "\n")
```

d. Access the 13rd to 18th elements and 33th to 35th elements of worker’s Age.
```{r}
# Ages vector
ages <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 
          35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 
          50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 
          35, 24, 33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 
          48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)

# Access 13th to 18th elements
elements_13_to_18 <- ages[13:18]

# Access 33rd to 35th elements
elements_33_to_35 <- ages[33:35]

# Combine both ranges into a single selection
combined_elements <- ages[c(13:18, 33:35)]

# Print results
cat("13th to 18th elements:", elements_13_to_18, "\n")
cat("33rd to 35th elements:", elements_33_to_35, "\n")
cat("Combined selection:", combined_elements, "\n")
```

e. Access all but the 10th, 20th, 30th and 40th elements are not included.
```{r}
# Ages vector
ages <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 
          35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 
          50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 
          35, 24, 33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 
          48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)

# Extract specific ranges using index concatenation
subset_ages <- ages[c(13:18, 33:35)]

# Display the extracted vector
subset_ages
```

f. Modify the 4th, 14th, 24th, and 44th elements with value = 0.
```{r}
# Ages vector
ages <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 
          35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 
          50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 
          35, 24, 33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 
          48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)

# Modify the specified indices to 0
ages[c(4, 14, 24, 44)] <- 0

# Display the modified vector
ages
```


Question 2:

R has actually lots of built-in datasets.
For example, the rivers data “gives the lengths (in miles) of 141 “major” rivers in North America, as compiled by the US Geological Survey”.
Use data(rivers)

a. Get the number of elements (length) in rivers, their sum (sum), mean (mean), median(median), variance(var), standard deviation(sd), minimum (min) and maximum (max).

```{r}
# Load the built-in dataset
data(rivers)

# Calculate summary statistics
len_rivers  <- length(rivers)
sum_rivers  <- sum(rivers)
mean_rivers <- mean(rivers)
med_rivers  <- median(rivers)
var_rivers  <- var(rivers)
sd_rivers   <- sd(rivers)
min_rivers  <- min(rivers)
max_rivers  <- max(rivers)

# Print all results
cat("Length (n):", len_rivers, "\n")
cat("Sum:", sum_rivers, "\n")
cat("Mean:", mean_rivers, "\n")
cat("Median:", med_rivers, "\n")
cat("Variance:", var_rivers, "\n")
cat("Standard Deviation:", sd_rivers, "\n")
cat("Minimum:", min_rivers, "\n")
cat("Maximum:", max_rivers, "\n")
```
b. What is the result? The derived result must be in just one(1) vector name.
```{r}
# Load rivers data
data(rivers)

# Calculate summary statistics into a single named vector
rivers_stats <- c(
  Length = length(rivers),
  Sum    = sum(rivers),
  Mean   = mean(rivers),
  Median = median(rivers),
  Var    = var(rivers),
  SD     = sd(rivers),
  Min    = min(rivers),
  Max    = max(rivers)
)

# Display the single vector result
rivers_stats
```

Question 3: The table below gives the 25 most powerful celebrities and their annual pay as ranked by the editions of Forbes magazine and as listed on the Forbes.com website.

a. Create vectors according to the above table.

```{r}
# Create Power Ranking vector (1 to 25 based on the list order)
power_ranking <- 1:25

# Create Celebrity Name vector
celebrity_name <- c(
  "Tom Cruise", "Rolling Stones", "Oprah Winfrey", "U2", "Tiger Woods", 
  "Steven Spielberg", "Howard Stern", "50 Cent", "Cast of the Sopranos", 
  "Dan Brown", "Bruce Springsteen", "Donald Trump", "Muhammad Ali", 
  "Paul McCartney", "George Lucas", "Elton John", "David Letterman", 
  "Phil Mickelson", "J.K Rowling", "Bradd Pitt", "Peter Jackson", 
  "Dr. Phil McGraw", "Jay Lenon", "Celine Dion", "Kobe Bryant"
)

# Create Pay vector (in millions)
pay <- c(
  67, 90, 225, 110, 90, 332, 302, 41, 52, 88, 55, 44, 55, 
  40, 233, 34, 40, 47, 75, 25, 39, 45, 32, 40, 31
)

# Combine into a single data frame (table representation)
celebrity_data <- data.frame(
  Power_Ranking = power_ranking,
  Celebrity_Name = celebrity_name,
  Pay = pay
)

# Display the data frame
celebrity_data
```
b. Modify the power ranking and pay of J.K. Rowling. Change power ranking to 15 and pay to 90.

```{r}
celebrity_name <- c(
  "Tom Cruise", "Rolling Stones", "Oprah Winfrey", "U2", "Tiger Woods", 
  "Steven Spielberg", "Howard Stern", "50 Cent", "Cast of the Sopranos", 
  "Dan Brown", "Bruce Springsteen", "Donald Trump", "Muhammad Ali", 
  "Paul McCartney", "George Lucas", "Elton John", "David Letterman", 
  "Phil Mickelson", "J.K Rowling", "Bradd Pitt", "Peter Jackson", 
  "Dr. Phil McGraw", "Jay Lenon", "Celine Dion", "Kobe Bryant"
)

power_ranking <- 1:length(celebrity_name)

pay <- c(
  67, 90, 225, 110, 90, 332, 302, 41, 52, 88, 55, 44, 55, 
  40, 233, 34, 40, 47, 75, 25, 39, 45, 32, 40, 31
)

# Find the index for J.K. Rowling
jk_index <- which(celebrity_name == "J.K Rowling")

# Modify power ranking and pay
power_ranking[jk_index] <- 15
pay[jk_index] <- 90

# Verify the changes
data.frame(
  Name = celebrity_name[jk_index], 
  Power_Ranking = power_ranking[jk_index], 
  Pay = pay[jk_index]
)
```
Question #4:

Create a list of ten (10) vegetables you ate during your lifetime. If none, just list down the vegetables in your mind.

Answer: "Carrot", "Broccoli", "Spinach", "Potato", "Tomato", "Cabbage", "Cucumber", "Onion", "Garlic", "Eggplant"

a. Add 2 additional vegetables after the last vegetables in the list. What is the result?

```{r}
# Original vector (12 vegetables from previous step)
veggies <- c("Carrot", "Broccoli", "Spinach", "Potato", "Tomato", 
             "Cabbage", "Cucumber", "Onion", "Garlic", "Eggplant", 
             "Pumpkin", "Squash")

# Add 2 additional vegetables after the last element
veggies_updated <- c(veggies, "Bell Pepper", "Zucchini")

# Display the updated vector
veggies_updated
```

b. How many datapoints do you have?

Answer: 14 datapoints

c. Add 4 additional vegetables after index 5. What is the result?
```{r}
# Current vector (14 vegetables)
veggies_updated <- c("Carrot", "Broccoli", "Spinach", "Potato", "Tomato", 
                     "Cabbage", "Cucumber", "Onion", "Garlic", "Eggplant", 
                     "Pumpkin", "Squash", "Bell Pepper", "Zucchini")

# Insert 4 additional vegetables after index 5
veggies_final <- append(veggies_updated, c("Lettuce", "Radish", "Celery", "Corn"), after = 5)

# Display the resulting vector
veggies_final
```
